correctness.rationale: The domain is finite and exhaustively covered: every connected cubic bipartite graph of order 12 corresponds to a 6-by-6 binary matrix with all row and column sums 3. The verifier enumerates all 550 nondecreasing-row semilabeled matrices, quotients exactly by all row permutations, canonical column sorting, and transpose, and obtains five connected classes. It checks every candidate dominating matching. Four classes have a dominating 2-matching; the fifth has none but has a dominating 3-matching. A separate exact LCF construction identifies the fifth class as Franklin. The lower bound gamma_pr>=4 follows because one edge in a simple cubic bipartite graph dominates exactly six vertices. No probabilistic, floating-point, timeout, or partial-search premise is used.

value.rationale: The initiating 2026 theorem makes equality structure a natural next question and explicitly discusses equality witnesses. Order 12 is the first new multiple-of-four order after the cube where the sharp value 6 can occur. The complete five-class classification shows that equality persists but is exceptional, selecting the named Franklin graph uniquely; this is a structurally interpretable finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of a known table. The result supplies an exact benchmark for any future equality characterization.
